assessments.reasoning: I reacquired the exact Computer History Museum-hosted ACM scan. Its title identifies the revised author report and the scan DOI resolves in ACM-deposited Crossref metadata to Communications of the ACM 6(1), January 1963. The left column of physical and printed page 12 limits the equivalence model to bodies written in ALGOL. Section 4.7.3.2 replaces each formal absent from the value list with its corresponding actual throughout the body. It uses parentheses at syntactically permitted sites and systematic changes to involved formal or local identifiers to avoid conflicts with the inserted identifiers. Section 4.7.4 establishes positional pairing on matching arity. Section 4.7.5 restricts well-formed replacements, including requiring a variable actual for a non-value formal used as an assignment target. The value-formal rule, subsequent body-insertion rule, and treatment of non-ALGOL bodies are consistent with the claim boundary.

challenge.method: Read fresh rendered pages 12 and 13. Tried to disprove the claim by switching the formal into the value list, passing a computed expression to a non-value formal used as an assignment target, supplying a non-ALGOL body, and considering whether an inserted identifier could bind to a same-named callee local. Compared sections 4.7.3.1 through 4.7.3.3, 4.7.4, 4.7.5.2 and 4.7.8.
challenge.results: Value-list membership takes the value-assignment branch. An assignment-target formal omitted from that list requires a variable actual, so a computed non-variable expression cannot refute the scoped claim. Non-ALGOL body restrictions fall outside the reference language. For valid substitution with a callee-local collision, section 4.7.3.2 calls for a systematic identifier change. The extra renaming at body insertion has a distinct trigger. The exact claim survives all four controls.

limitations: This is the January 1963 report model for an ALGOL procedure body at a valid call. The report describes equivalent execution effects, leaving compiler strategy outside this assessment.
The changes in section 4.7.3.2 address conflicts caused by actual substitution inside the body. Section 4.7.3.3 separately addresses call-site conflicts arising at body insertion.
